user_prompt: Is the core idea of this paper novel relative to the related work I gave you?
scope: The target paper target/paper.txt (arXiv:1512.03385, Deep Residual Learning) and the supplied corpus of 10 real related-paper abstracts under corpus/, searched by search_repo and read by inspect_file; the novelty question is scoped to the target's STATED contribution and to subsumption BY THE SUPPLIED CORPUS ONLY (not the open literature).

claims.text: The target paper's stated contribution is identifiable from the supplied text (a residual learning framework that reformulates network layers as learning residual functions, via parameter-free identity shortcut connections, to ease training of substantially deeper networks).
The contribution is identified (C1) and the closest work in the supplied corpus has been located by search and inspected.

Under the supplied corpus and the declared search protocol, no inspected corpus item subsumes the target's stated contribution (parameter-free identity shortcut connections that let a layer learn a residual function against its input, with no learned gating and no auxiliary per-layer loss, enabling networks over 100 layers deep to be trained and to gain accuracy from depth): the contribution stands as novel relative to this corpus.

atoms.proposition: The target's contribution paragraph is read via inspect_file over target/paper.txt.
The corpus is searched for the mechanism family with search_repo (pattern residual|shortcut|deep network|very deep over corpus/), returning at least one match.
The closest gated-shortcut corpus candidate (Highway Networks, arXiv:1505.00387) is read via inspect_file.
The closest deep-training-aid corpus candidate (Deeply-Supervised Nets, arXiv:1409.5185) is read via inspect_file.
Expert adjudication is obtained (ask_user) on whether any inspected corpus abstract claims the target's specific mechanism; the adjudication is that none does.

notes_for_annotators: Target arXiv:1512.03385 (ResNet, He et al. 2015), corpus of 10 real abstracts, all fetched 2026-07-29 from arxiv.org abs pages (provenance in artifacts/res-resnet/PROVENANCE). ADJUDICATION (E5 answer, verified by reading the abstracts): No corpus item subsumes the target's stated contribution. The target's contribution is a PARAMETER-FREE identity-shortcut reformulation -- 'reformulate the layers as learning residual functions with reference to the layer inputs' -- trained with a single end-to-end objective, scaling cleanly to 152 layers (and 100-1000 on CIFAR-10). The closest corpus items differ in mechanism: Highway Networks (1505.00387, 2015) also eases very-deep-network training via shortcut-like information flow, but through LEARNED GATING UNITS ('the use of gating units which learn to regulate the flow of information') -- extra transform/carry-gate parameters at every layer, not the target's simple parameter-free addition; Deeply-Supervised Nets (1409.5185, 2014) eases deep-network training by adding a 'companion objective' (auxiliary classification loss) AT each hidden layer -- a fundamentally different mechanism (multi-loss supervision, no shortcut connections at all) from the target's single-objective identity-shortcut reformulation. Neither prior work proposes gate-free identity shortcuts trained with one end-to-end loss at 100+ layer depth. VGG (1409.1556) and GoogLeNet (1409.4842) are deep/wide plain- or inception-module architectures without any shortcut mechanism; Batch Normalization (1502.03167) and Network In Network (1312.4400) address different training/architecture aspects (internal covariate shift; 1x1-conv micro-networks); Rethinking Inception (1512.00567) is a concurrent inception-family paper (no shortcuts); Identity Mappings in Deep Residual Networks (1603.05027) is the target's OWN follow-up, postdating it (March 2016 vs December 2015); FCN (1411.4038) and R-CNN (1311.2524) are unrelated downstream application architectures (segmentation, detection) with no depth-training mechanism proposed. Route minimality: E1 necessary (cannot judge novelty without reading the contribution); E2 necessary (the corpus must actually be searched, not assumed); E3, E4 necessary (the two nearest candidates must be read, not inferred from titles); E5 necessary (the subsumption call is the adjudicated conclusion). Order-coherence by containment. Decoy citation_count_lookup is not a listed action. The answer the ask_user tool returns is this note; E5 attests that the adjudication was obtained.
